---

I'm prototyping a medium-heavy economic euro board game called **Entrepreneurs** and I
need a complete set of print-and-play components. I'll print them at home on A4 and US
Letter, cut them by hand and play on a table - so design for *that*, not for a factory.

Build me a **design system first, then the components**, as separate artboards I can
print one per sheet.

## What the game is

2–6 players build companies in a 4×4 city of districts. Every company pays a bill each
quarter to companies in *other* industries - its suppliers - and those payments are the
heart of the game. Building a company pushes its own industry's price down $1 and each of
its suppliers' prices up $1, so the market is the sum of what the table has built.

The game is 8 quarters over 2 years (a three-year variant plays 12). Each quarter has three
phases: **Planning** (place workers), **Action** (tracks resolve, take actions) and
**Closing** (bills and rent are paid, every company collects its tier, the industry pots
are shared, a Logistic Hub opens; at Q4 and Q8 the land awards and the loan buy-back).
A second Megacorp calls the following quarter as the last one.

**How a company earns.** It counts the demand icons of its industry it can reach and
collects the best of three tiers printed on its card that it *fully* meets: enough icons
AND a market price at or above the one printed. Otherwise it collects the Minimum. The
amounts are printed in dollars - nothing is multiplied at the table.

The tone should be **corporate-modern, not sci-fi and not cute**: an annual report or an
architect's site plan rather than a cartoon city. Clean, confident, information-dense but
legible across a table at arm's length.

## Non-negotiable constants

These are the game's actual values. Do not invent, round, or "improve" them.

**Six industries.** The colours are checked in CIE Lab against the three colour-vision
deficiencies (worst pair 27.3 apart); use them exactly.

| Code | Name | Colour | Base price | Grows | Running cost | Entry grade |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UT | Utilities | `#D9C70D` | $4 | Horizontal (spreads) | Low | Easy |
| RE | Retail | `#5DD067` | $4 | Vertical (stacks) | High | Medium |
| HO | Hospitality | `#DA421D` | $5 | Vertical (stacks) | Low | Easy |
| MA | Manufacturing | `#744BAA` | $5 | Horizontal (spreads) | Mid | Hard |
| HC | Healthcare | `#324DE1` | $6 | Vertical (stacks) | High | Hard |
| TE | Technology | `#DD61B0` | $6 | Horizontal (spreads) | Mid | Medium |

**Accessibility is the most important constraint.** Give every industry a second,
redundant channel - a distinct logo or glyph - and print its two-letter code beside it
wherever the industry appears. A player must be able to play the whole game in greyscale.

**Player colours** (up to 6): `#1B8FB3` `#D06A10` `#7B61D9` `#D9416B` `#2E9E57` `#A37F00`. A disc shows *who*, a block
shows *what*, so a disc must never be read as an industry: pair the player colour with a
shape or a ring, never colour alone.

**Price track:** $2 to $12, one marker per industry, one cell per whole dollar. Mark each
industry's base price.

**Other values:** 12 discs per player · 5 company bays (a sixth with the IPO tile) · 3 EP the first time
a player builds in an industry · 2 EP a level when built and again when upgraded · cash scores 1 EP per
full $100 · loans $20 for a disc, −5 EP each unpaid, bought back for $30 at the end of
Year 1 and $40 at Year 2 ($50 at Year 3 in the three-year game) · land awards at each year end
to the outright leader in plots built on and in districts stood in: 4 EP + the player count
(6 at two seats, 10 at six) · 2 Megacorps call the end · a Megacorp HQ banks its industry's
price ÷ its tile's tier as EP every quarter and pays 1 EP a quarter to each rival company beside it.

## The supplier web

Every industry buys from exactly three others and sells to exactly three others; 12
of the eighteen links run both ways. Draw it as a real graph, not a ring.

```
UT buys from  HO, MA, TE        RE buys from  UT, MA, HC
HO buys from  UT, RE, HC        MA buys from  RE, HC, TE
HC buys from  RE, HO, TE        TE buys from  UT, HO, MA
```

## Pay: the supplier bill

A company pays its suppliers one round total each quarter, set by its industry's running
cost and its level; every level doubles it. One supplier takes all of it, two take half
each, and a card that starts at Level 3 prints three suppliers: the first takes half and
the other two a quarter each. Upgrading doubles what each supplier is paid.

| Running cost | Industries | Level 1 | Level 2 | Level 3 | Level 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Low | Utilities, Hospitality | $5 | $10 | $20 | $40 |
| Mid | Manufacturing, Technology | $10 | $20 | $40 | $80 |
| High | Retail, Healthcare | $15 | $30 | $60 | $120 |

## Earn: the three tiers

the industry is to enter. The icon counts are per company level; the price is the market
price the industry's marker sits on.

## Rent

A company standing on another player's plot pays that owner, per floor, $1 for every full
$5 the plot is worth (never less than $1). A plot is worth its road price plus $3 for each
structure on it or orthogonally touching it. Nothing is owed on your own land.

## The components I need

### 1. The city board
A 4×4 grid of **16 districts**. Each district is a 3×3 block in which **4 of the 8 compass
positions hold a plot** and the centre never does - the centre carries the district's name
and its demand grid. **64 plots** in all. Two plots are neighbours if they are orthogonally
adjacent on the underlying 12×12 grid, across district borders too, so never draw districts
as tidy 2×2 blocks. The four centre districts are always FC, IA, CC and LM, shuffled into the
middle 2×2; twelve of the 16 suburb tiles are drawn for the ring.

The **road prices** are fixed by position and can be printed on the board: the 9×9 lattice
below sits over the district grid (even rows and columns are roads; "." is a district's
middle). A corner plot reads its district's corner, an edge plot the middle of that edge.

```
1 1 2 1 2 1 2 1 1
1 . 3 . 3 . 3 . 1
2 3 4 3 4 3 4 3 2
1 . 3 . 5 . 3 . 1
2 3 4 5 6 5 4 3 2
1 . 3 . 5 . 3 . 1
2 3 4 3 4 3 4 3 2
1 . 3 . 3 . 3 . 1
1 1 2 1 2 1 2 1 1
```

a **4×4 grid of demand icons**: four rows, one industry each, and four columns numbered 1–4 -
the company level that counts that column. **All four rows are open from the first
quarter.** The first and last rows are always the same industry. Nothing is ever placed on
an icon: players count them, so the grid only has to read clearly across the table.

### 3. Sixty Blueprint cards
Poker size (63×88 mm), nine to an A4 sheet with cut marks. Ten per industry: five that start
at Level 1, three at Level 2, two at Level 3. Each card shows, in this order of importance:

- **Earn:** the three tiers - Minimum, then each tier's icons, price and amount.
- **Pay:** each supplier (logo + code) and the amount it is paid.
- Name, industry, **level**, and whether it spreads or stacks.
- **Build:** the cost and how many owned plots it needs; the EP it scores when built.
- **Upgrade:** the cost again plus one more owned plot (spreading) or floor (stacking), and
  the EP it scores. Every number that changes on upgrade is printed after a slash, in grey:
  the upgraded tiers, the upgraded bill.
- **Sell / liquidate:** what the card fetches in hand, and what the company fetches built.

The full card list is the appendix at the end.

Claimed by merging an exact combination of company levels. Each shows a name, the
combination, a one-off EP award and a **tier from 1 to 4**. The tier is a *divisor*: the
headquarters banks its industry's price ÷ tier as EP every quarter. **Tier 1 is the best.**
Make the divisor as prominent as the EP.

### 5. Six persona cards
One dealt to each player; the rest sit out.

- **Systems Architect** (TE) — Your Technology companies may upgrade vertically, stacking on one plot instead of needing a free neighbour - or spread as Technology usually does. You choose at each upgrade.
- **Public Health Director** (HC) — Your Healthcare companies reach every column of a Healthcare row whatever their level - they may count all four icons where a level-1 company counts one.
- **White-Label Supplier** (MA) — Your Manufacturing may be paid the best price among the rows of its own district, its own row included: that is the price its tiers are checked against.
- **Resort Developer** (HO) — Your Hospitality companies may upgrade horizontally, spreading across plots so more businesses and hubs sit adjacent to them - or stack as Hospitality usually does. You choose at each upgrade.
- **Supply Chain Expert** (RE) — At the start of Closing, you may raise one industry you do NOT operate by one step; your Retail then reaches one extra district this quarter. You may also decline.
- **Concession Holder** (UT) — At the start of Closing you may switch your concession on: your Utilities then read the market price as $1 higher this quarter - the higher price is the one their tiers are checked against. Every quarter you are paid at that premium, the Utilities price falls one step at the end of the quarter.

### 6. Money
Printed notes, about 44 × 88 mm, 8 or 12 to an A4 sheet: **$1, $2, $5, $10, $20, $50**. Bills
come in fives, so the $5 and $10 are the busiest notes; make all six easy to tell apart by
colour, size and number position together.

### 7. Player pieces (printed fallbacks; I 3D-print the rest)
- **12 discs per player.** A disc under a building marks who owns the *land*; a disc on top
  marks who owns the *business*.
- **Company blocks, levels 1–4** - stack height reads as level.
- **A Megacorp HQ marker**, a **Logistic Hub** token (one a quarter) and **Retail branch** tokens.
- **2 workers per player** (3 at a two-player game).

### 8. Action tracks
Workers are placed **left to right**; each track resolves **right to left**, and a worker takes
one action plus one for every worker placed after it. Make both directions visible on the board.

- **Raise Capital** (LOAN, SELL), **M&A** (BUY, LAUNCH), **R&D** (RESEARCH, UPGRADE) - 4 slots each at
  2–4 players, 5 at five, 6 at six.
- **Board Meeting** (GO PUBLIC, REPOSITION) - always 2 seats, the second opening with the IPO tile.

### 9. Player aid (double-sided, one per player)
Front: the three phases, with Closing as a checklist - bills and rent, every company collects
its tier, Megacorp dividends and tithe, the pots are shared, the hub, the year end. Back: the
supplier web, the bill table, the rent rule and the scoring summary.

### 10. Small bits
A **quarter track** of 8 (Q4 and Q8 marked as year ends with the land awards and the buy-back;
Q9–Q12 dashed for the three-year variant), an **EP track**, **loan tokens**, a **first-player marker**, and
the **IPO tile** (to the first player to form a Megacorp: a sixth company bay and Board
Meeting's second seat, no EP).

1. **A design system artboard first** - palette with the exact hexes above, the six industry

4. **No bleed, visible cut lines**, generous inner margins.
